classes.name: Вибори народних депутатів України (чергові та позачергові)
classes.name_en: Verkhovna Rada general elections
classes.finest_note: Polling station (виборча дільниця) from 2006 on the Commission's sites; single-member district in 1998 and 2002.
classes.note: Unicameral, 450 seats (Constitution art. 76). The Verkhovna Rada of the Ukrainian SSR elected on 4 March 1990 in 450 single-member districts (runoffs 18 March) is the first convocation. 1994: 450 majoritarian districts with a 50% turnout rule, so many seats stayed empty and were refilled in repeat elections through 1996. 1998 and 2002: mixed, 225 list seats (4% threshold) and 225 single-member districts. 2006 and the early 2007 vote: closed-list PR in one nationwide district (3%). 2012 and the early 2014 and 2019 votes: mixed again (5% threshold); in 2014 and 2019 the districts in occupied Crimea and parts of Donetsk and Luhansk did not vote (198 and 199 districts). The Electoral Code (2020) moves to 450 seats by open-list PR in 27 regional districts with a 5% threshold, not yet used. Martial law, in force since 24 February 2022, bars elections while it lasts (Law «Про правовий режим воєнного стану», art. 19), so the regular dates that fell due under it were not held. The regular election due on 29 October 2023 was not held.

classes.name: Вибори Президента України
classes.name_en: Presidential elections
classes.finest_note: Polling station on the Commission's sites (vp1999 to vp2019); territorial district on the oldest pages.
classes.note: Two-round majority vote; the top two meet in a runoff three weeks later when no candidate wins a majority of the votes cast. The post was created by the law of 5 July 1991. Runoffs: 10 July 1994, 14 November 1999, 21 November 2004 (annulled by the Supreme Court and repeated on 26 December 2004), 7 February 2010, and 21 April 2019; 1991 and 2014 were decided in the first round. Martial law, in force since 24 February 2022, bars elections while it lasts (Law «Про правовий режим воєнного стану», art. 19), so the regular dates that fell due under it were not held. The regular election due on 31 March 2024 was not held.

cadence.runoff_rule: The two leading candidates meet on the third Sunday after the first round when no one wins more than half of the votes cast.
cadence.vacancy_rule: An early election within 90 days; the Chair of the Verkhovna Rada acts meanwhile (art. 112).

classes.name: Всеукраїнські референдуми
classes.name_en: All-Ukrainian referendums
classes.finest_note: Oblast and territorial district on the 2000 referendum site (r001).
classes.note: The Ukrainian SSR's vote of 17 March 1991 put the all-Union question on preserving the USSR and the republic's own question on the Declaration of State Sovereignty. The independence referendum of 1 December 1991 confirmed the Act of Declaration of Independence. The referendum of 16 April 2000, called by popular initiative, put four questions on constitutional change that were never enacted. Constitution arts. 72-74; the 1991 law on all-Ukrainian and local referendums, its 2012 successor (struck down by the Constitutional Court on 26 April 2018), and Law No 1135-IX of 2021, under which no referendum has been held. A referendum on territorial changes must be national (art. 73).

classes.name: Вибори депутатів обласних рад
classes.name_en: Oblast council elections
classes.finest_note: Council and electoral district on the Commission's local sites; polling-station figures stay with territorial commissions.
classes.note: Oblast councils (oblast soviets until 1994) are elected for five years (Constitution art. 141; four years before 2006). Systems: majoritarian districts in 1990-2002, closed lists in 2006, mixed in 2010, lists with candidates assigned to territorial districts in 2015, and open lists in 2020. Oblast governors head appointed state administrations and are not elected. No oblast council elections were called in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts in 2015 or 2020. Martial law, in force since 24 February 2022, bars elections while it lasts (Law «Про правовий режим воєнного стану», art. 19), so the regular dates that fell due under it were not held. The regular local elections due on 26 October 2025 were not held.

classes.note: Kyiv's council, 120 seats since 2006. Early elections were called on 25 May 2008 and 25 May 2014, so Kyiv held no council election in 2010. Martial law, in force since 24 February 2022, bars elections while it lasts (Law «Про правовий режим воєнного стану», art. 19), so the regular dates that fell due under it were not held.

classes.name_en: Kyiv mayoral elections
classes.finest_note: City; the Commission's sites list the elected head.
classes.note: Two-round majority vote since 2015 (runoff 15 November 2015; won outright in 2020). Whether the 1994 vote for the chair of the city council counts as Kyiv's first mayoral election was not settled from a fetched source, so the class starts in 1999. Martial law, in force since 24 February 2022, bars elections while it lasts (Law «Про правовий режим воєнного стану», art. 19), so the regular dates that fell due under it were not held.

classes.note: Sevastopol's council; the city's executive was an appointed state administration. No election under Ukrainian law has been possible since the 2014 occupation; votes the occupying power organizes are the occupied_votes class.

classes.name: Вибори депутатів Верховної Ради Автономної Республіки Крим
classes.name_en: Verkhovna Rada of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea elections
classes.finest_note: Council and electoral district on the 2010 local site.
classes.locator: https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/254к/96-вр (art. 136: the Verkhovna Rada of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea)
classes.note: Crimea's 100-seat parliament (Supreme Council of Crimea until 1998), elected in 1994 with the national parliament, in 1998, 2002, and 2006 with it again, and in 2010 with the local elections. The 1990 Crimean oblast council, which became the Supreme Council in 1991, is counted with the oblast councils. No election under Ukrainian law has been possible since the 2014 occupation.

dates.note: Runoffs 10 April 1994.

classes.name: Вибори Президента Республіки Крим
classes.name_en: President of the Republic of Crimea election
classes.note: Crimea's only popular vote for a president of its own, 16 January 1994 with a runoff on 30 January 1994; the Verkhovna Rada abolished the post on 17 March 1995.

dates.note: Runoff 30 January 1994.

classes.disposition_reason: Run by Crimea's own election commission before the Central Election Commission existed; no official results publication survives online, so it needs an archival or printed official source.

classes.name: Вибори голів обласних і районних рад 1994 року
classes.name_en: Direct elections of oblast and raion council chairs (1994)
classes.note: Under the February 1994 local elections law, voters elected the chairs of oblast and raion councils directly on 26 June 1994, with runoffs; the 1995 Constitutional Agreement and the 1996 Constitution returned the choice to the councils. Not settled from a fetched source.
classes.disposition_reason: Declared by oblast and raion commissions before the Central Election Commission existed; no official results publication is online.

classes.name: Місцеві референдуми та дорадчі опитування
classes.name_en: Local referendums and consultative polls
classes.note: The 1991 law on all-Ukrainian and local referendums allowed oblast, raion, and community referendums: the Crimean referendum of 20 January 1991, the Galician oblasts' independence question of 17 March 1991, Transcarpathia's autonomy question of 1 December 1991, and the Donetsk and Luhansk consultative polls of 27 March 1994 among them. Law No 5475-VI of 2012 repealed it without a local referendum law to follow, so no local referendum has had a legal basis since.

dates.note: Local referendums and polls under the 1991 law; no central list.

classes.disposition_reason: Run and declared by local councils' commissions with no central publisher; results survive only in local official gazettes and archives.

classes.name: Вибори до Верховної Ради Української РСР (1938-1985)
classes.name_en: Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian SSR elections, 1938-1985
classes.note: Eleven single-candidate elections under the 1937 and 1978 republican constitutions (1938, 1947, 1951, 1955, 1959, 1963, 1967, 1971, 1975, 1980, 1985). The competitive 1990 election opens the rada class.

dates.note: Eleven general elections; not counted from an official list.

classes.disposition_reason: Results survive only in the republic's printed gazettes and archives; there is no machine-readable official source.

classes.name: Вибори до місцевих рад депутатів трудящих (народних депутатів) Української РСР
classes.name_en: Local soviet elections of the Ukrainian SSR, 1939-1987
classes.note: Single-candidate elections of oblast, raion, city, settlement, and village soviets every two years (two and a half after 1977). The competitive local elections of 4 March 1990 open the local classes.
classes.disposition_reason: Results survive only in printed gazettes and archives; there is no machine-readable official source.

classes.name: Вибори до Верховної Ради СРСР та З'їзду народних депутатів СРСР в Українській РСР
classes.name_en: USSR Supreme Soviet and Congress of People's Deputies elections held in the Ukrainian SSR
classes.note: Elections of all-Union bodies in the republic's districts, up to the Congress of People's Deputies of 26 March 1989.
classes.disposition_reason: They elected bodies of the USSR, not of Ukraine; they belong to a Soviet Union census, not this one.

classes.name: Вибори до Українських Установчих Зборів
classes.name_en: Ukrainian Constituent Assembly election (1917-1918)
classes.note: Called by the Central Rada's Third Universal; voting in late December 1917 and January 1918 was completed in only part of the country before the Bolshevik offensive, and the assembly never met. The Central Rada itself was formed by delegation, not by popular vote.
classes.disposition_reason: Partial returns survive only in contemporary press and archives; there is no official results publication.

classes.name: Голосування, організовані державою-окупантом на тимчасово окупованих територіях
classes.name_en: Votes organized by the occupying power in occupied territory
classes.note: The 16 March 2014 Crimean vote and every later vote the occupying power or its proxies have run in Crimea, Sevastopol, and occupied parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson oblasts. Ukrainian law treats them as void.
classes.disposition_reason: Not held under Ukrainian law or by Ukrainian authorities; the archive records Ukraine's own elections in its territory.

classes.name: Вибори делегатів Курултаю кримськотатарського народу
classes.name_en: Kurultai of the Crimean Tatar people delegate elections
classes.note: The Crimean Tatar people's own representative assembly, recognized by the Verkhovna Rada in 2014, whose delegates are elected by Crimean Tatars under the Kurultai's own rules; the Kurultai in turn elects the Mejlis.
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the community's own institutions, not by the state or under an election law.

classes.name: Органи самоорганізації населення
classes.name_en: Residents' self-organization bodies
classes.note: House, street, quarter, and village committees chosen at residents' meetings under the 2001 law on residents' self-organization bodies.
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen at meetings, not by ballot under an election law.

classes.name: Обрання та призначення посадових осіб Верховною Радою
classes.name_en: Officers elected or appointed by the Verkhovna Rada
classes.note: The Chair of the Verkhovna Rada, the Prime Minister and Cabinet, members of the Central Election Commission, and other officers chosen by parliamentary vote (Constitution art. 85), and the presidium and executives chosen by local councils.
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by a body, not by voters.

classes.name: Призначення суддів
classes.name_en: Judges
classes.note: Judges are appointed by the President on the High Council of Justice's submission (art. 128 since 2016; until then the Verkhovna Rada elected judges for life). Constitutional Court judges are appointed in thirds by the President, the Verkhovna Rada, and the Congress of Judges.
classes.disposition_reason: No judge is chosen by popular vote.

classes.name: Висування кандидатів партіями
classes.name_en: Party nominations
classes.note: Parties nominate candidates and lists at their own congresses and conferences; the Electoral Code provides no state-run primary.
